result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-032.md: no-show reason capture, asked once with no reminder -- the FINAL requirement of Release 1 and of Phase 7. Issue #35's title ('Chapter interest wishlist') is misleading; that scope belongs to Release 3 per the issue's own release-boundary text, confirmed by reading it directly. REQ-032's actual scope is STORY-DETAILS D3 / PRD 13 AC8's no_show half.

SCHEMA CHECK (Sec0, mandatory) -- NO CHANGE IS NEEDED, unlike REQ-031's own cycle. `registrations.no_show_reason` already exists: a plain nullable `text` column, no CHECK, added by REQ-011's own migration (apps/bot/drizzle/0001_tired_annihilus.sql) and already described in REQ-011.md Sec5's derivation table as 'a real stored column, sharply distinguished from the derived, columnless no_show boolean.' Confirmed by inspection that nothing in apps/bot/src currently reads or writes it -- this requirement is its first consumer. One NON-BLOCKING confirmation question is routed to DATA-DESIGNER: keep the single free-text column storing EITHER one of five fixed NoShowReasonCode literals (work_ran_over/illness/forgot/transport/lost_interest) OR raw free text (this design's own recommendation, Sec1.1), or split into a reason_code/reason_free_text pair for cleaner PRD FR-16 factsheet aggregation by category. No CHECK constraint is proposed for the fixed set -- a closed-set CHECK cannot coexist with the same column also accepting arbitrary free text.

ASKED-ONCE MECHANISM (design question 2) -- CONFIRMED: the existing notification_ledger UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) constraint alone is sufficient, no separate asked-at column needed anywhere, unlike REQ-031's broadcast_opt_in_asked_at. Traced explicitly why the two cases differ: REQ-031 needed a durable column because users.broadcast_opt_in's own two values (true/false) cannot distinguish never-asked from asked-and-declined. no_show_reason has no such collision -- NULL unambiguously means not-yet-answered (never sent, or sent with silence -- STORY-DETAILS D3 treats both identically). The only state actually needing a once-only guarantee is 'was this send already attempted,' which is exactly what sendLedgeredNotification's own ledger insert already guarantees with zero new schema.

THE DERIVATION (design question 3) -- isNoShow placed in domain/registration.ts (not event.ts, where isFinished actually lives, confirmed by inspection) since its inputs are registration-shaped (admission, checkedInAt) not event-only-shaped, following this codebase's own convention of registration-state predicates living alongside decideRegistrationOutcome/decideWithdrawOutcome/etc. Exact boolean logic stated as a first-match-wins rule table (never as executable code, per the zero-implementation-code rule): admission==='admitted' AND checkedInAt===null AND endsAt!==null AND evaluationTime strictly after endsAt -> true; every other combination -> false, including the endsAt===null case (treated as undeterminable, not assumed true) -- a detail the requirement text's own shorthand omits but REQ-011 Sec5's derivation table already anticipated.

INTERACTION PATTERN (design question 4) -- five inline-keyboard buttons (one per fixed NoShowReasonCode) plus a sixth 'other' button; tapping a fixed-reason button writes its literal code directly (no free text needed, no disambiguation problem -- callback_data already carries the registration id). Tapping 'other' sends a force_reply prompt carrying ONE ref line ('No-show ref: <registrationId>') -- explicitly reasoned why this is a STRICT SUBSET of REQ-031 Sec3.1's two-line ref+field mechanism, not a full copy: REQ-031's field-disambiguation problem (which of several sibling fields a reply answers) does not apply here since there is only one free-text slot per registration, but REQ-031's more basic problem (which REGISTRATION a bare reply belongs to, since the same person can hold more than one admitted-not-checked-in registration across events) still applies unchanged, so the ref line is still required, just without a second 'field' line.

SCHEDULED JOB (design question 5) -- ONE job only (not two, unlike REQ-031), the fourth and final Release-1 consumer of scheduler/runner.ts. Selection query mirrors selectRegistrationsForFeedbackRequest's table style with checked_in_at IS NULL as its mirror-image clause (AC1's entire mechanism), admission='admitted', events.status='published', ends_at<=evaluationTime, and the same bounded CATCH_UP_WINDOW reasoning REQ-031 Sec5.2 already established. No NOT EXISTS ledger clause is added to the selection query itself (unlike REQ-031's reminder query) -- there is no second job here needing to exclude already-engaged candidates; the ledger's own UNIQUE constraint plus a send-time no_show_reason!==null recheck are what prevent any duplicate ask, which is also the entire mechanism behind AC3's T+24h/T+48h re-run test.

All 7 ACs mapped to concrete design elements in Sec6. Provisional-wording disclosure (AC7) stated explicitly in Sec5.1, mirroring REQ-014.md Sec1/Sec5 item 4's exact treatment -- BACKEND-DEV's own Step 2 handoff result.issues must record the no-show wording as provisional pending the product owner, per the requirement text's 'Viktor should write it' framing (no version marker proposed, unlike REQ-014's consent wording, since no scenario here requires distinguishing wording versions on already-answered rows). 4 open questions stated explicitly in Sec8: the schema shape confirmation (non-blocking); the CATCH_UP_WINDOW constant's size; the callback_data byte budget being exactly at the 64-byte cap for the longest reason code string (flagged for BACKEND-DEV to re-verify Telegram's byte-counting rule); a completeness-only note that the AC1 gate is already precisely as the requirement text states.
result.next_action: DATA-DESIGNER: read Sec0 of docs/agents/design/REQ-032.md and answer the one non-blocking confirmation question (single no_show_reason column, this design's recommendation, vs. a reason_code/reason_free_text split) -- record the decision in a short docs/agents/design/REQ-032-schema.md note (or confirm no schema artefact is needed if the single-column recommendation is accepted as-is). Unlike REQ-031, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR is NOT blocked on this: this design is fully buildable against the existing schema regardless of DATA-DESIGNER's answer, since registrations.no_show_reason already exists. Once DATA-DESIGNER responds (or explicitly declines to change anything), route both to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b).
